title: Vision-Based Vehicle Speed Estimation
summary: AI-powered computer vision system that detects vehicles and estimates real-time traffic speeds from video feeds without specialized hardware.
problem: Traditional speed monitoring relies on expensive radar/LIDAR hardware, making widespread traffic analytics costly for municipalities.
solution: Engineered an end-to-end computer vision pipeline using Python and OpenCV that performs object detection, centroid tracking, and pixel-to-meter perspective transformation for speed estimation.
features: Real-time vehicle detection and bounding-box tracking using optical flow and centroid analysis
Perspective calibration mapping pixel displacements to physical real-world metric distances
Automated speed calculation with visual violation alerts and speed statistics output
architectureDetails: Preprocessing stage: Frame differencing, noise reduction, and region-of-interest (ROI) filtering
Tracking & Measurement: Multi-object centroid tracker with velocity vector calculation per frame interval
metricsOrOutcome: Accurate non-intrusive vehicle speed detection from standard video camera feeds
